prompt_text: Who is the best roofer in Denver for hail damage repair?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: I can’t name one single “best” roofer for Denver without current local research, but I can help you find the best contractor for your situation and tell you exactly how to vet them. If you want, give me your ZIP code and I’ll pull together top-rated options and check their credentials.

Quick checklist to find the best Denver roofer for hail damage
- Get at least 3 written estimates from different contractors.
- Verify license/registration and insurance (general liability + workers’ comp).
- Confirm they are experienced with hail repairs and with insurance claims.
- Look for manufacturer certifications (GAF, Owens Corning, CertainTeed) — these matter for shingle warranties.
- Check recent Google/Yelp reviews, BBB rating, and ask for local references (last 6–12 months).
- Check for a written workmanship warranty and manufacturer shingle warranty details.
- Make sure they will obtain permits and provide a final inspection.
- Avoid high-pressure “storm chaser” contractors who appear after a storm and demand large up-front cash; insist on a clear contract and lien waivers.

Important questions to ask a roofer
- Are you licensed/registered in Colorado and insured? Can you provide certificates?
- Do you have experience with hail claims in Denver? Any local references?
- Will you handle the insurance estimate/meet with the adjuster?
- What brands and warranties do you offer on shingles and labor?
- What is the project timeline and payment schedule?
- Who does the work — employees or subcontractors?
- Will you obtain permits and clean up / remove debris?

Red flags
- Contractor asks you to sign over your insurance check.
- No physical address or only a cell phone number.
- Pushy sales tactics, “today-only” pricing after a storm.
- No proof of insurance or unwillingness to provide references.

If you want, I can:
- Look up the top-rated hail-damage roofers in Denver (give me your ZIP) and list 4–6 candidates with ratings, certifications, and contact tips.
- Draft an email or text you can send to contractors requesting estimates.
- Walk you through handling the insurance claim and the adjuster meeting.

Which would you like me to do next? (If you want a local list, please share your ZIP code.)
